links.reason: Both state the brevity of life (இனிச்செத்தாம் பிறந்த போழ்தே; பெற்ற வாணாள் இத்துணை என்பது ஒன்றும் அறிந்திலம்), so the pairing is a shared claim, not a development. The note misreads 2616: கறந்து கூற்று உண்ணும் ஞான்று is Death milking and drinking the life, not a cow being milked. Nothing in 2939 marks it as passing on Vijayai's words, so the 'doctrine passed down' claim in teaches is unsupported.
links.text_issue: 2939 lines 3-4 are compressed and hard to construe (தனிச்சித்தம் வைத்தல் தேற்றாம்)

links.reason: Both are the heroine telling her friend that the promised season has come (காலை வந்தன்றால் காரே; கார்மன் இதுவால்), and the colophons do give பாலை and முல்லை. That is one situation in one domain, so parallel_domain does not fit. The colophon point in teaches is true (183 opens with அத்தம்ஆர் அழுவம், 194 is all field-work), but it is an observation about the anthology's labels more than a link between the poems.
links.text_issue: 194 line 1 'வகைறை' looks like a misprint for வைகறை

links.reason: 820 names the battlefield sin and its removal outright (போர்கெழு களத்துப் பாவம் புலம்பொடு போக்கினானே). 2357 only has the king bow to the Lord, scatter gold and put on collyrium, garland and ornaments (முனைவற் றொழுது ... செம்பொன் கொளவீசி), with no word of sin, lament or expiation. Reading the morning adornment as the same rite of expiation imports 820 into a verse that does not support it.

2806 has the gods take their fill of fortune without being sated (திருவொடு திளைத்தும் ஆனார்), and that is related to the turn from pleasure. But verse 29 gives its own reason: having tasted something sweeter (தேன் வாய் உமிழ்ந்த அமிர்து உண்டவன் போன்று), he no longer wants the lesser pleasure, not that pleasure fails to satisfy. Verse 29 is also in the patikam, not at the opening of an ilampakam as the note says.
links.text_issue: 2806 line 4 ஆனார் / மானார் division is uncertain

links.reason: The link rests on one word, ஏதிலர் / ஏதிலார. In 1130 the town calls him loveless (இகந்துறைவர் ஏதிலர்); in 1300 the maxim says strangers cannot be one's own when one's own heart is not (நெஞ்சம் தமரல் வழி). These are not incompatible claims about the same thing. 'The outsider is inside' is wordplay on the shared word.

The contrast is real. Kattiyangaran answers Civakan's taming of Asanivegam with the brand of 'thief' (கள்வர் என்ன எழுதுவித்திடுவல்), and the assembly in 1840 answers his mastery of an elephant with acclaim (குஞ்சரக்கு உரியவன் இவனலால் உலகினில் இலன்). But the two verses do not make incompatible claims, which tension requires. It is a contrast of courts across two episodes, and the note's 'king's must elephant' and 'lawful king' come from the story, not from 1840.

Kural 638 is about the minister's duty to speak even when the king destroys counsel (அறிகொன்று அறியான் எனினும்). In 146 the ministers advise and the king listens (நரபதியுங் கேட்டனன்), so the couplet's case never arises. The 'false premise' belongs to the ministers' own staged death of the queen, so the king is deceived by his advisers, not misled by honest counsel. Nothing in the verse tests or limits the rule.

The two verses share no image. What joins them is the usurper's hypocrisy: the false tears at the pyre (கரிமாலை நெஞ்சினான் ... கைதொழுதான் கண்ணீர் கலுழ்ந்து) and the letter's protest of false blame (பொய்ப்பழி பரந்தது என்மேல்). That is a real link, and it is better typed as develops: a lie the narration has already exposed. The claim that Govindan sees through it 'at once' goes beyond 2144.

265 looses the hounds as if to seize red flesh (செந்தசைகள் சென்றுகவர்கின்றென விடுத்தான்), and 279 says they do not come near (ஞமலி இவை நணுகல), through the greatness of the ascetic's yoga. This is an act and its reversal, which develops covers; the two verses make no incompatible claims. The link sits close to plain story order, so it is thin.

134 ends with the merchant saying he does not know the cause (காரணம் யானறியேன்), and in 137 Dharanisundari says where the women came from and that Vayuvegan asked their father for them (கருதியெம்மைக் கேட்டனன்). That is a question answered in story order, and 137 does not yet give the cause of the singing. 'A wrong that the hero is to put right' is not in either verse.

1360 likens Civakan leaving the sleeping Padumai to a good life leaving the body (உடம்பு நீங்கி நல்லுயிர் போவதே போல்), and 1122 likens the lovers' bond to body and life (உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை). The shared image is real, and turning the union into a departure is a fair point. But the body-and-life simile is common stock, and nothing in 1360 develops the couplet's claim, so same_image fits better.

The contrast in teaches is true of the words. The Charana's litany takes in சங்கரன் ஈசன் சயம்பு சதுமுகன் and வேத முதல்வன் (186, 189), while Cintamani 1 keeps to தாவாத இன்பம் ... தன்னின் எய்தி and ஓவாது நின்ற குணத்து. But neither text limits the other, so qualifies is the wrong type. 'Bare definition' is also strong for one invocation verse that itself uses the title தேவாதி தேவன்.

Both heroines address a household bird in love-grief, so the bird as confidante is a shared figure. But 1000 only has the parrot ask Gunamalai to name the man (சமழாது உரை); it does not fly as her envoy. And 1364 names only the myna (பூவையொடும் புலம்பி), not a swan, peacock and lamp. The rule in teaches, that the messenger exists only while the lover is within reach, is the proposer's generalisation.

2623 contrasts those who ate milk-rice from gold bowls with those who eat greens from a potsherd (அடகிடுமின் ஓட்டகத்து), and ends 'do not think of wealth, think of the tapas done' (செல்வம் நமரங்காள் நினையன்மின் செய்தவமே நினைமின்). That is wealth's instability. Naladiyar 273 is about the hoarder who neither enjoys nor gives (துய்த்துக் கழியான் துறவோர்க்கு ஒன்று ஈகலான்). The connection is only the shared theme of wealth, and the 'banquet temptation of ease' in gains is invented.
links.text_issue: 2623 line 3 is hard to divide (அடகிடுமின் ஓட்டகத்து)

links.reason: Kural 698 tells those who serve a king not to slight him as young or as kin (இளையர் இனமுறையர் என்று இகழார்). Pradyotan's letter pleads kinship (மாமனான் மருகன் நீ), but not to slight anyone and not as a minister. It is one king appealing to another, so the couplet's case is absent. Joining them rests on the shared idea of kin degree alone.

2240's dead have paid the red-rice debt (செஞ்சோற்றுக் கடன் நீங்கி), and jackals howl over them (இனநரியோடு ஓரி நின்று அலறும்). Kural 780 measures a death by the patron's tears (புரந்தார்கண் நீர்மல்க) and says nothing of a debt. So the 'Kural's logic of a death owed' in teaches and the epic-side gain are not in the couplet. The absent patron set against the jackals is a real contrast, but a thin one.

79 gives youth that kindles love-fire in women (காமநோய் எரிவளைத்திடுவதோர் இளமை), and TM 180 gives a man once desired as cane and now bitter as காஞ்சிரங்காய். Placing them on one arc is a fair reading of the pair, but it is the familiar theme of youth's impermanence. The other-side gain is false, because TM 180 already contains its own beginning (விரும்புவர் முன்என்னை).

1186 proposes matching means, art against art for the Vidyadharas and men against men without deceit (வஞ்சனை இன்றி மக்கள் பொருபவேல் மக்கட் போரே). Puram 9 proclaims who is to be sent to safety before the arrows (ஆவும் ... பெண்டிரும் பிணியுடையீரும்). Both put limits on war, but neither qualifies the other, and 'both limit war' is only the shared theme.

Both have the wedding drum beaten for the public (பல்லார் அறியப் பறையறைந்து; கடிமுரசு அறைவான்), so this is a shared image. But Naladiyar 86 uses the drum to argue against looking at another's wife, and 2388 is only the proclaimers dressed and set on an elephant. The 'moral weight' in the epic-side gain and the 'seven days of orders' in the other are not in the verse.

2371 is a pure enthronement picture (சிங்காசனத்தின்மேல் சிங்கம்போல் ... இருந்தான்), with no hint of a turning wheel or of a fall to come. The warning comes entirely from Naladiyar 3. The other-side gain is false, because the quatrain already has the rival as agent (மனையாளை மாற்றார் கொள).

1217 names Civakan by the earlier act itself (செல்கதி மந்திரஞ் செவியிற் செப்பிய), which is 945's whispering of the five mantras into the dying dog's ear (மந்திரம் ஐந்தும் ... செவிச் செப்புகின்றான்). The god's gift of three mantras repays it, so this is a deed and its fruit, signalled in the words. Teaches is accurate.

The shared word is exact: Kural 363 makes வேண்டாமை the highest wealth here and hereafter, and Pazhamozhi makes it the means to everything wanted (வேண்டாமை வேண்டியதெல்லாம் தரும்), applied to the king's servant who asks nothing (வேண்டுதும் என்பது உரையற்க). Turning the renouncer's virtue into court strategy is a real application, and teaches names it precisely.

429 only shows an unnamed king fanned on the lion throne holding a water lily (அரியாசனத்து இருந்தான்). The raid and the failure to guard are in other verses. Kural 560's ஆபயன் குன்றும் is the decline of the cows' yield under a neglectful guardian, not a cattle raid. The political reading of the raid as 'first public proof' goes beyond what this verse says.

The overlap is anger (வெகுளி போக்குக; காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம்). Beyond that, the verse lists practices and the couplet lists faults, which is complementary at most, and neither limits the other. Both gains clauses say what each side lacks, not what it gains.
links.text_issue: kural 360 'இநவ்முன்றன்' is a corrupt print of இவ்மூன்றன்

links.reason: Kural 618 says lack of fortune is no one's disgrace (பொறியின்மை யார்க்கும் பழியன்று), and Pazhamozhi 236 forbids calling the unrewarded petitioner dull or small (தேற்றார் சிறியர் எனல்வேண்டா) because gain comes by lot. The application to the court is exact. Teaches rightly notes that the Kural's second half, the blame for want of effort, is dropped.

1827 has the rejected kings console themselves that deeds ripen as they will (வினைகடாம் விளையுமாறு யாம் வேண்டியவாறு வாரா). The poet's chapter-close in 1839 turns the same doctrine into a moral for all (வினையதனின் விளைவு இன்னது என்று நாளும் நினைமின்). A character's thought is taken up as the narrator's teaching, which is a development. 1839 frames it as the fruit of merit rather than the bearing of loss, a slight shift.

Soolamani 33 also crosses the tracts. The kurinji from the hill women's millet field (கொடிச்சியர் புனத்தயல் குறிஞ்சி) is worn by the ghee-selling herdswomen, and the kuvalai the farm women weed (கடைச்சியர் களையெறி குவளை) is in the hair of the shore women (கானல்வாய்த் தொடுத்து அலர் பிணையலார் குழலுள்). The contrast in teaches, which says the epic keeps each woman with her own flower, misreads the verse. The pair is closer than the note says.
links.text_issue: 33 line 2 கதுப்பயர் கமழும் மேழையம் is obscure

links.reason: 225 has the king explain the good omens and stop short of the rest (பின்னதனால் பயன் பேசலன் விட்டான்). 267 has him say that all she dreamt that night has come to pass (கங்குல் நீ அன்று கண்ட கனவு எல்லாம் விளைந்த). That is a dream and its fulfilment, with the withheld part admitted, so the link is sound.

Naladiyar 16's image is the lamb nibbling the garland in the slaughter-ground (மறி குளகு உண்டன்ன). Yasodhara 20 only lists pairs of peacocks, cocks, pigs, goats and buffalo brought by the king's order (மன்னன் ஆணையின் ... இரட்டைகள்). There is no garland, no grazing and no unawareness, so the shared image is only 'sacrificial animal'. The epic-side gain admits it adds what the verse does not say.

The distinctive image is the same in both: சிலந்திநூல் தன்னால் ஆர்த்த சிங்கம்போல் (211) and சிலந்தி நூலிற் செறித்த நற்சிங்கம்போல் (60). Both apply it to Udayanan's capture, first in the narration of Vayantakan's letter and then in the captor's own apology. Teaches is accurate.

The two verses agree that pleasure binds: காமத் தொங்கலாற் பிணிக்கப்பட்டார் (2840) and போகத்தால் விழுங்கப்பட்டுப் புறப்படான் (2610). There is no incompatibility, so tension is the wrong type. Teaches states the link well.

The cart wheel is really shared (ஓடுஞ் சகடத்து உருளும்; சகடக்கால் போல வரும்), and teaches correctly separates wealth turning from the soul turning. The other-side gain reads karma and rebirth into Naladiyar 2, which gives a different reason: share wealth because it does not stay level (அகடுற யார்மாட்டும் நில்லாது).

Yugi's use of the enemy king's own elephant to free the captive fits the couplet's 'one deed made the means of another' (வினையான் வினையாக்கிக் கோடல்), and the verse does order the destruction of army and city (சேனைமன் நகர் அழித்து). But the elephant here shakes off its chain (அருந்தளை உதறிற்று) rather than binding another elephant. So the other-side gain, the couplet's image 'acted out', is false.

The crows at the opened body are really shared (கண்ணுள் காக்கை; காக்கை கடிவதோர் கோல்), and 1584 does turn the image on the woman before him (கொடியே என்றான்). The epic-side gain, that it lets the rebuff be brief, is not specific and not true of a dense four-line catalogue. The other-side gain is speculation about stock figures.
links.text_issue: 1584 lines 2-3 (தடிதடித் கீழ்ந்த; பிள்ளையார் கண்ணுட் காக்கை) are probably corrupt

links.reason: 1669 has the king go to watch the women bathe (கடிபுனலாடல் காண்பான்), and 1674 has the water-play begin (மயங்கமர் தொடங்கினாரே). That is consecutive story order with no answer, fulfilment or reversal beyond the scene moving on.

1628's closing question (இன்னகைப் புதல்வர் செல்வம் யாவரே இனிதென்னாதார்) is a proverbial aside on the plant-wedding, and it does not engage the Kural's reason (தம்தம் வினையான் வரும்). Making the tree a test of whether children's deeds are the reason stretches a figure of speech into an argument neither text makes.

347 does name a former-birth deed (உம்மை நின்றது ஓர் ஊழ்வினை) and brings Vijayai to the tapas grove (தவப் பள்ளியே). Kural 378, though, is an ironic claim that fate will not let the destitute renounce (உறற்பால ஊட்டா கழியுமெனின்). 347 does not say she renounces. The 'following verses' and 'the Kural answers in the negative' in teaches and gains go beyond both texts.

The only shared element is the word for dream (கனா; கனவாச்சே). 106 reports a prophetic dream, and Pattinattar's line says all he saw became a dream once he became open space (வெட்டவெளி யானேன்). One is about omen-reading and the other about the unreality of the seen, so they are not incompatible claims about the same thing.

1981's one life in two bodies (ஈருடம்பு ஓருயிர் ஆயினார்) and 1122's body-and-life bond are related lover images. But விட்டு நீங்குதல் இன்மையின் gives a cause, that they never left each other, and does not set a condition, so 'conditional on never parting' strains it. The 'pledge' and 'breach' in teaches and gains are not in the narrator's line.

233's order to build a rare machine (ஓர் அரும் பொறி புனைவி) is fulfilled in 272 (ஊர்தி சமைந்தது), so an order and its execution are linked. That is close to story order. Teaches calls the machine 'penance', which Wisdom's words do not say; she offers it as a last means after the lost senses (ஓதிய பொறி அற்றாய்).

The verse fits the couplet's warning about heedlessness, but the order of events is not what teaches says. He walks on past the omens and Vayantakan's check (புள்ளிடை தடுப்ப ... வயந்தகன் விலக்கப் போந்து) before he sees the elephant and grows glad (யானை கண்டே ... இனியன் ஆனான்). So the gladness does not cause the slackness. The 'joy's slackness' (உவகை மகிழ்ச்சியிற் சோர்வு) is applied loosely.

TM 145 is about the body's impermanence: the town wails, renames the man a corpse, burns him and forgets (நினைப்பொழிந்தார்களே). 141 is the king's grief at burnt ornaments with no body (கரிப்பிணத்தைக் காண்கிலர்). The idea that 'lament follows belief, not fact' is drawn from neither text, and the song gains nothing from a staged death.

2701 is the conventional picture of women spent after love-play (செவ்வாய் விளர்த்துத் தோண்மெலிந்து ... அசைந்தார்), with no hint of decline. Naladiyar 17 is about age bending the spear-eyed woman (கோல்கண்ணள் ஆகும் குனிந்து). Reading the pallor of love as 'early decline' stretches the verse to meet the quatrain.

a rhetorical boast in question form, not a claim
